title: Heuristic inquiry docket — ad-hoc eval notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick brain dump while triaging a weird regression on long-form summarization workload (customer: internal staging). Not polished — personal scratchpad.

Summary of observable: 
- Model variant: open-llama-13b-q4 (served via hosted)
- Regression: increased factual hallucination rate around tokens 150-300 in summaries produced for long inputs (>4k tokens). Previously (baseline July) most hallucinations concentrated near tail; now spikes mid-output.
- Hypothesis: cache eviction / KV mismatch when prefix tokens exceed 3k and runtime switches to alternate kernel path. Could also be a prompt-context shuffling issue introduced by batching changes in release 2024-11.

Quick checks ran: 
- Run small batch (n=8) with same seed across 2024-10 snapshot vs current: 5/8 regress vs 1/8 before.
- Forced single-request (no batching): drop of hallucination events by ~40% in quick sample (n=10).
- Reproduced locally with quantized weights + caching disabled: regressions persist.

Ad-hoc rubric (for quick triage scoring, 0-3):
- factuality: 0 = severe halluc, 1 = small fact slip, 2 = minor paraphrase, 3 = faithful
- attribution: 0 = fabricated cite, 1 = unreliable claim, 2 = vague but plausible, 3 = explicit supported
- coherence: 0 = jumpy/contradict, 1 = odd tangent, 2 = minor drift, 3 = coherent
- brevity-violations: 0 = vastly verbose, 3 = within expected length

Example annotated sample (prompt truncated):
INPUT: long policy doc ~5.2k tokens (meeting notes + annex)
OUTPUT excerpt (tokens ~180-240): 
- "According to section 4.2 the vendor agreed to a 60-day SLA and deposit of $500k" 
Rubric scoring: factuality=0 (section 4.2 only mentions escalation, no SLA), attribution=0 (fabricated $ figure), coherence=2 (sentence is grammatical but false), brevity=3
Notes: pattern = wrong numeric figures inserted, often round numbers.

Observations / signals: 
- Hallucinations tend to be round-dollar figures (50k, 500k, 1M) or precise-looking dates.
- When the model emits a citation-like phrase ("section 4.2"), confidence of statement is high in text but unverifiable.
- Token positions 150-300 correlate with first long-form synthesis pass in our staged decode pipeline (we do a chunk-then-merge).

Immediate experiments to run (short list):
1) Disable chunk-then-merge flow and stream full-context summarization single-pass — check if halluc spike shifts. (Ticket: JIRA-ML-2314)
2) Run same workload with batching disabled at the router level for 1 hour to check throughput vs hallucation tradeoff. (A/B vs canary)
3) Add a quick heuristic to reject numeric tokens that do not appear in source text (post-process check) and measure impact on quality and false-positive suppression rate.
4) Test older kernel path (pre-release 2024-11-02) vs current.

Notes for later: 
- Might be related to KV cache aliasing when chunk boundaries align with attention window resets. If so, adding unique chunk separators (token blends) might reduce aliasing.
- Cross-check embeddings similarity between generated numeric phrase and nearest source spans — if low, likely halluc. Could incorporate as a signal for candidate rewrite.

Open questions / quick TODOs: 
- Is this present across other model variants (redwood-small, redwood-base)? Quick run pending. 
- Which CI/regression tests would have caught this? We need a small end-to-end long-input fidelity test in hosted smoke that runs weekly. (Add to repo under test/e2e/long-fidelity)
- Who to rope in: @Asha for rubric tuning, @Rae for kernel/runtime insights, SRE for adding temporary canary routing.

Scratch log of commands run (local):
- python eval/compare_snapshots.py --model open-llama-13b-q4 --snapshots 2024-10-01,2024-11-12 --dataset long-summary-staging --seed 42 --n 20
- curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/generate -d '@sample_long.json' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REPRO' (batching toggled off)

Slack / references: 
- slack: #evals (thread: "mid-output halluc spikes")
- GH PR for batching change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve/pull/987 (note: runtime batching switching logic modified)
- Quick confluence draft for reproducibility steps: confluence:evals/playbook-2024 (private)

Brainstorm mitigation ideas (short):
- Lightweight post-filter for numerics and named entities derived from source tokens.
- Conservative decoding temperature in the mid-output stage (adaptive temp schedule).
- Chunk separators + explicit markers to avoid KV aliasing.
- Add perimeter prompt instruction: "Do not invent numbers not present in the text" — measure instruction-following reliability.

Closing notes (stream-of-conscious):
- This feels operational-runtime-adjacent rather than purely model-quality; big suspicion on the kernel switch and batching heuristics. 
- Prioritize quick A/B disabling batching and run an automated rubric pass to quantify regression size across customers. 
- Save this as working artifact, will formalize if we can reproduce on deterministic runs.

-- Noah R.
